abstract: Can a company use copyright law to keep damning footage from public view when it was obtained through repeated trespasses?
summary: The High Court of Australia ruled that a constructive trust over copyright cannot be used to suppress public interest information. Game Meats, the abattoir, claimed Farm Transparency had unlawfully obtained footage of animal welfare breaches. The court found that while damages were insufficient, transferring copyright to Game Meats went too far, as it would restrict third-party rights and public interest disclosures. The HCA rejected the use of a constructive trust to identify third-party recipients of the film and threaten them with infringement proceedings.
title: High Court of Australia not too game on copyright constructive trusts that suppress information in the public interest
